claim.markdown_says: ## 14.9.30.3 Syntax rules   (H2 - while the immediately preceding siblings on page 722 are '### 14.9.30.1 General' and '### 14.9.30.2 General formats', and the parent is '## 14.9.30 READ statement')
claim.why_it_matters: The Syntax rules clause is hoisted to the same outline depth as the READ statement clause that contains it, so it detaches from READ in any TOC/outline and splits the statement's four sub-clauses across two levels. Neighbouring statements are transcribed correctly ('### 14.9.29.3 Syntax rules', '### 14.9.31.3 Syntax rules').

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed, with the claim's supporting facts checked one by one against both sources. PDF page 723 (printed folio 693) opens with the bold clause heading '14.9.30.3   Syntax rules' followed by 'ALL FORMATS' and syntax rules 1)-12); PDF page 722 (folio 692) carries '14.9.30 READ statement', '14.9.30.1 General' and '14.9.30.2 General formats'. In specs/ISO_COBOL.md the four clauses are transcribed at inconsistent depths: line 29441 '## 14.9.30 READ statement', 29444 '### 14.9.30.1 General', 29449 '### 14.9.30.2 General formats', 29499 '## 14.9.30.3 Syntax rules', 29545 '## 14.9.30.4 General rules'. Every quotation in the claim is exact. Named neighbours check out: 29410 '### 14.9.29.3 Syntax rules' and 29827 '### 14.9.31.3 Syntax rules' are both H3. Rejection grounds were tested and none apply. (1) Nothing is missing: the heading text, the clause number and all twelve rules are present and correctly worded, so the 'missing-heading' label is a misnomer - the defect is a wrong heading LEVEL. (2) Not mere formatting: in a numbered standard the markdown heading level is the only machine-readable carrier of the clause containment tree, and the dotted number 14.9.30.3 unambiguously subordinates it to 14.9.30. At H2 it becomes a sibling of READ rather than its child, so any outline, TOC generator or section-extraction pass (including this repo's spec-lookup navigation) resolves it outside the READ statement. (3) Not a deliberate house convention: H3 is the dominant transcription pattern for fourth-level clauses (35 '### 14.9.N.3 Syntax rules' versus 14 at '##'), and decisively, the inconsistency is INTERNAL to a single statement - .1 and .2 at H3 but .3 and .4 at H2 within 14.9.30 - which no convention could produce. One nuance the claim states loosely: the PDF's typography does not itself distinguish level 3 from level 4 (14.9.30, .1, .2 and .3 are all set in the same bold face and size); the depth is carried entirely by the dotted clause number, which is unambiguous. That does not weaken the finding. The claim also understates the scope.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, but mislabelled and under-scoped. Correct kind is 'wrong-heading-level', not 'missing-heading': no text is absent from the transcription - the heading '14.9.30.3 Syntax rules', its anchor 'section-14-9-30-3' and all twelve syntax rules are present and faithful. The defect is that specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29499 emits the clause as H2 ('## 14.9.30.3 Syntax rules'), making it a sibling of its own parent '## 14.9.30 READ statement' (line 29441) instead of a child alongside '### 14.9.30.1 General' (29444) and '### 14.9.30.2 General formats' (29449). Scope is larger than claimed: '## 14.9.30.4 General rules' (line 29545) carries the identical defect, so READ loses two of its four sub-clauses, not one. Further, this is a systemic transcription pattern rather than an isolated page-723 slip - about 40 fourth-level clauses across section 14.9 are emitted at H2 (14.9.1.3/.4, 14.9.2.3/.4, 14.9.4.3, 14.9.10.4, 14.9.11.4, 14.9.12.4, 14.9.13.3/.4, 14.9.14.3/.4, 14.9.18.4, 14.9.19.4, 14.9.20.4, 14.9.22.3/.4, 14.9.23.4, 14.9.24.4, 14.9.25.4, 14.9.26.4, 14.9.27.4, 14.9.28.3/.4, 14.9.30.3/.4, 14.9.37.3/.4, 14.9.38.4, 14.9.39.3/.4, 14.9.40.3/.4, 14.9.44.3/.4, 14.9.48.4, 14.9.49.3/.4, 14.9.51.3/.4), against 35 transcribed correctly at H3. Any repair should be a document-wide sweep normalizing four-component clause numbers to H3, not a one-line edit to page 723. Finally, the claim's phrase 'printed in the same style as 14.9.30.1' is true but not itself the evidence of depth: the PDF sets 14.9.30, .1, .2 and .3 in one identical bold face, so subordination is established by the dotted clause numbering alone.
